summary: Presence analytics no longer fragments a continuous drive into one trip per ~2-minute polling tick. A trip's trailing edge now gets the same quiet-boundary protection a stay's arrival already had, using Life360's own is_driving signal.
details: RawFix gains is_driving (Life360's own per-fix motion signal, 100% filled) as the primary settlement signal, with a settled_seconds time-based fallback and a max_trip_duration_seconds safety valve against a stuck signal.
The fix watermark now holds back an undecided trailing group of fixes rather than consuming them, so a drive spanning many polling ticks correctly settles into one trip once it actually ends.

A stationary subject's trailing fixes are recognized as a stay-in-progress once they've dwelled past the existing stay-arrival threshold, rather than waiting on a settlement clock that Life360's resting cadence never lets elapse — closing a second fragmentation path found while fixing the first.
limitations: The 9 trip rows already written in production before this fix remain fragmented as they are — new drives from deploy onward extract correctly, but nothing backfills or re-derives the earlier ones.

A related, unconfirmed question was surfaced but not addressed here: whether the existing open-stay mechanism has an analogous cross-tick timing property for a stay's own arrival time. Flagged for separate investigation, not fixed in this change.

The watermark-holdback mechanism has a real, bounded stall: if an entire batch holds back with no new fixes arriving, the watermark stays frozen until the backlog crosses the backfill threshold (on the order of 11 hours at a realistic driving cadence with default settings) before a wider batch drains it. Self-healing, but not instantaneous.

The corridor-clustering watermark (last_cluster_id) is not held back alongside this fix's watermark. Assessed as benign (no path found where a written trip escapes clustering) but not proven exhaustively.
